yes, you can start tagging images and later rerun imageRename to add the next batch of images to outDir
The function will not overwrite existing images in outDir. Just make sure you don't rename any renamed images after running imageRename, otherwise the function will copy these images and there will be duplicates.

Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Detection histories with multiple setup and retrieval dates per camera
messages.subject_clean: Detection histories with multiple setup and retrieval dates per camera
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Once again - many thanks for this awesome package. I am currently trying to reconcile a combination of my own understanding of survey techniques and processing data for occupancy analyses. I am working with data from a camera trap grid where cameras are repeatedly deployed over multiple sessions (generally reset monthly - sample of CT table attached). From my reading of current topics, I'm not really sure how to account for multiple setup and retrieval dates for each camera when trying to calculate aggregated detection rates across the 9 or so months that the cameras have been deployed in various configurations. I've added a session column to keep track of the different trapping bouts at this stage but I'm not clear on how I should incorporate them. I've been following some of Juergen's suggestions and provided code from this post <https://groups.google.com/d/msg/camtrapr/Dlotf_6xB_s/bFVV6GK6DAAJ>. I've also reattached the functions that Juergen provided.

So - in effect - I want to create a composite detection history for my species of interest (elephants) over the duration of this project. On average, the cameras were deployed for between 30 and 40 days at a time. However, when I try to calculate a detection history for elephants, I encounter an error stating that not all values of stationCol in recordTable are matched by rownames of camOp. This makes sense since the camera names have been appended with _sessionX after the cameraOperation step and therefore they're not matching up. However, I'm really stuck on understanding how to proceed to create the composite detection history based on the per camera trapping effort. Do I just need to rename the camera stations in the recordTable with their session number such that they match up with the operation matrix? Any guidance on how to account for this multiple session trapping in the generation of detection histories (ideally for downstream usage in occupancy analyses) would be extremely appreciated.

I've attached samples of code, a sample recordTable, and the station matrix as well. Thank you in advance!

Best,
Patrick

messages.subject: Re: problem with exiftool
messages.subject_clean: problem with exiftool
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a similar problem. I had already worked with Exiftool and R previously without problems, but recently it has started to produce problems (I don't know why, same code, same computer, and even the same photos!)

We have solved it with this code:

setwd('...photos directory...')
obj <- system2("...exiftool directory...", args="-common  -FNumber -DateTimeOriginal -FileType -csv -r ... photos directory...", stdout=TRUE)

Although we are not using camtrapR for that, I think that the problem can be similar and it can help you. This code generates an R object with the metadata of the photos.

Hoping that it helps
Pablo
